Course Overview & Editorial Methodology

This course introduces undergraduate students to computational philology, digital manuscript curation, and the production of scholarly digital editions. Bridging traditional humanities textual criticism with modern data science, you will learn how premodern manuscripts—from papyrus fragments to parchment codices—are transcribed, catalogued, collated, and published in the 21st century.

Most weeks follow our rigorous Three-Step Comparative Methodological Cycle:

  • Tuesday (Manual Foundations): We establish ground-truth reference standards by hand, examining physical codicology, scribal hands, and editorial decision-making.
  • Wednesday (Deterministic & Rule-Based Tools): We execute algorithmic, rule-based scripts and industry-standard tools (e.g., Git, IIIF APIs, CollateX, TEI/XML schemas, morphological parsers) measured directly against our manual reference.
  • Friday (AI-Assisted & Large Language Models): We evaluate modern foundation models and generative AI systems, auditing hallucinations, measuring error rates (CER/WER), and evaluating how probabilistic models augment computational scholarship.
